clue.text: Cleaner goes in car to get pickled fish

indicators.note: the cleaning tool goes in, so its letters sit inside the car's name

parts.note: a Rolls is a Rolls-Royce car
a mop is a cleaning implement

explanation.surface: Someone driving off with a cleaner in the car to buy pickled fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'goes in' places the cleaner inside the car. Rollmops are herring fillets rolled round a filling and pickled.
explanation.definitionFit: Rollmops are rolled herring fillets marinated in vinegar, a classic pickled fish dish.

clue.text: Recompensed for rise in baby linen

indicators.note: in a down clue, a rise means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: diaper is the cloth a baby wears, the American nappy

explanation.surface: Someone paid back for the going rate of baby clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise in' turns DIAPER upwards in this down entry, giving REPAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Having been recompensed is having been repaid what was owed.

clue.text: Deposit covers new bid that's reserved

indicators.note: one word covers the other, so the second sits inside the first

parts.note: to lay something down is to deposit it

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters of bid

explanation.surface: A deposit secures a fresh bid that has been set aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' scrambles the bid, and 'covers' has the deposit wrap round it. 'that's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laid by has been put aside for later, that is, reserved.

indicators.note: to reform is to shape again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A political shake-up of nominations in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnesota is one of the states of the USA, in the upper Midwest.

parts.note: read can as American slang for a jail rather than a tin or the verb

explanation.surface: A boast that an American is capable of anything.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation suggests can-do confidence; in American slang the can is a prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A penitentiary is a US state or federal prison, which American slang calls the can.

indicators.note: the first letter of the synonym is removed

parts.note: school forms are classes

explanation.surface: School forms run without a headteacher, full of girls.
explanation.walkthrough: Forms are school classes; 'with no head' drops the C of CLASSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasses is a Scottish and northern English word for girls or young women.

parts.note: a lack is a shortage of something

explanation.surface: A cry of dismay at running short.
explanation.definitionFit: Alack is an archaic exclamation of sorrow or regret, like alas.

indicators.note: the letters are put into play and moved about, as in a game

explanation.surface: Urging a tennis player to get on with it at set point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to play' rearranges SET POINT; the tennis picture hides the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Step on it is an idiom telling someone to go faster, from pressing the accelerator.

definitions.meaning: a trivia claim: this eight-letter word has only one syllable
might as a noun means power or force

explanation.definitionFit: Strength is power or force, the noun sense of might, and is famously a long single-syllable word.

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the place name is rearranged

explanation.surface: Feeling sentimental about a holiday in Paignton.
explanation.walkthrough: PAIGNTON is a seaside resort in Devon; 'about' rearranges its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Poignant means touching or deeply moving, stirring emotion.

definitions.meaning: to rush headlong, as a vehicle ... along

explanation.definitionFit: Career as a verb means to move swiftly and wildly; as a noun it is one's working occupation.

parts.note: read down-to-earth literally: a worker whose job is the soil itself, not a practical person

explanation.surface: Praise for a sensible, unpretentious working man.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm labourer works the land, literally dealing with the earth all day.

clue.text: Initially it may be uphill, even steep

indicators.note: the opening letters of the next five words are taken

explanation.surface: A warning that a climb may be uphill and even steep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steep' looks like part of the hill picture but is the definition, as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue is to soak or saturate, just as to steep something is to infuse it.

parts.note: a track is a rough path
coming from the summit means going down

explanation.surface: Locating a trail that leads off a mountain top.
explanation.definitionFit: To track down someone or something is to find them after a search.

clue.text: One who is out and about

definitions.text: One who is out and about

parts.words: One who is out and about
parts.note: read out as asleep, not as being socially active: someone wandering while unconscious

explanation.surface: A description of a sociable person who gets around a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleepwalker is out for the count yet walks about, so is literally out and about.

clue.text: Found out such appliances are dangerous

definitions.meaning: discovered, as something dug up is brought to light
electrical appliances lacking an earth wire are a shock hazard

explanation.definitionFit: Unearthed means discovered or dug up, and also describes electrical equipment with no earth connection.

clue.text: Fellow who's learned what's not relevant

definitions.meaning: a scholar, such as a university fellow
of only theoretical interest, as in a question that is purely moot

explanation.definitionFit: An academic is a scholar at a university, and an academic point is one of no practical relevance.

parts.note: in can mean during, as in in the war
action is military combat

explanation.surface: Soldiers accused of idling in the middle of combat.
explanation.walkthrough: In action means fighting, the very opposite of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Inaction is a lack of activity, the state of doing nothing, which is idleness.

indicators.note: putting the words in a new order rearranges their letters

explanation.surface: A notice that a contaminated site must be sealed off from the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges NO ADMITTANCE; 'required' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Contaminated means made impure or dirty by a harmful substance, as polluted water is.

parts.note: el is the Spanish masculine word for the
flat ground is even

explanation.surface: Asking the number of a Spanish apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like a Spanish home but means level.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleven is a number, the one after ten.

clue.text: In class it's hard to be virtuous

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, here the letter inside the social class

parts.note: a caste is a hereditary social class
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A pupil finding it difficult to be good in the classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure and morally virtuous, especially abstaining from sex.

clue.text: Pack freight in view on board

definitions.note: describes goods stowed where they can be seen on a ship

parts.note: a deck is a pack of playing cards
cargo is goods carried as freight

explanation.surface: Instructions to load freight where it can be seen on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Deck cargo is stowed on the open deck rather than in the hold, so it is visible on board.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo stowed on a ship's open upper level, rather than below, is plainly visible aboard.

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
a rush is a reed-like plant

explanation.surface: A career that crowds hurry to join.
explanation.walkthrough: Profession here means a declaration of faith, not a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a statement of belief, the sense of profession as in profession of faith.

indicators.note: the name is introduced into the words, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A man who first met ethics at university.
explanation.walkthrough: The name spans the join of mo-RAL PH-ilosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph is a man's name, and a fellow is a man.

clue.text: A girl to help people out

indicators.note: the people are on the outside, round the help

parts.note: men are people
aid means help

explanation.surface: A young woman who comes along to assist others.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden is an old word for a girl or young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Four in fresh search for for historical documents

indicators.note: the number goes inside the rearranged letters
fresh means made anew, so the letters of search are rearranged

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four people start a new hunt for old papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges the search into ARCHES, and 'in' puts the Roman four inside. The doubled 'for for' is a printed slip, read as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Archives are collections of historical records kept for reference.

indicators.note: in an across clue the girl's name comes on, after, the container

parts.note: a can is a vessel for holding liquid
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A country girl travelling aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country girl' reads as a rural lass; the definition is just Country.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada is a country in North America.

parts.note: a woman whose first name is a word meaning good judgment and caution

explanation.surface: A tactful woman who lives up to her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudence is a girl's name and also a noun meaning careful good judgment or discretion.
